The password security practice described in the text is highly insecure. Using the same password for every account is a major risk because if one account is compromised, all other accounts using that same password are immediately vulnerable. Although Sarah changes the password monthly, this does not mitigate the risk of a single breach exposing all her accounts. A better practice is to use a unique, strong password for each account, ideally managed with a password manager.

A group of crows is called a murder.
